Target Social Media Enrichment Options
Adds regional platform families on top of the default global sweep — RU adds VK, Odnoklassniki, LiveJournal and Habr; CN adds Weibo, Zhihu, CSDN and Gitee; US adds niche consumer sites (Venmo, Calendly, Amazon). Discovered profiles are then opened and mined for identifiers. Leave all unchecked for global platforms only.
RU also enables hh.ru as a company source for Live Analysis › Organization — corporate profile, subsidiary brands, departments, offices, open roles and recruiter contacts. The rest of that card (vendors derived from the domain's own DNS) needs no region.

Infrastructure
Proxy profile is disabled. Analysis and enrichment workflows run without proxy settings.
The managed Tor client listens inside the stack — workflows reach it as socks5h://ssh-tunnel-api:9050. The port is never published to the host.
Entry (guard) countries
none selected
Exit countries
none selected
Country selection is a preference, not a guarantee. Tor honours ExitNodes reliably; EntryNodes competes with guard pinning, so a chosen entry country may be ignored for the life of the current guard set. Strict nodes turns both into hard requirements — circuits then fail outright rather than leaving the selected countries, which is safer for attribution and worse for reliability. Selecting nothing lets Tor choose freely, which is the least fingerprintable option.
Tor status unknown — click Refresh Tor status.
OPSEC
Applies to outbound analysis and enrichment requests. The egress check at the top of this page uses the same values, so what it reports is what a target would log.
A stale browser build or a stack whose parts disagree (Chrome UA from a Linux host) is more distinctive than the default, not less. Match the User-Agent to the story the rest of the egress tells.
Overrides the resolver the platform uses for name lookups it makes itself — the OPSEC point is to keep target lookups off the host / ISP / corporate resolver. Domain recon resolves over DoH, so it honours Cloudflare or Google (and any JSON-style https://…/dns-query URL under Custom); a resolver it can't reach that way is recorded and skipped, never silently sent to the default. This does not apply when egress is proxied through SOCKS5 or Tor: socks5h:// already resolves DNS at the proxy, which is the stronger guarantee.
SSH SOCKS5 Tunnel
SSH password and key passphrase are available for runtime actions, but are not persisted when saving this profile. The managed tunnel API token is supplied by the gateway — it is no longer entered here.
Select auth mode explicitly to avoid ambiguous credential handling. The key path is read inside the tunnel sidecar, where SSH_KEY_DIR is mounted at /ssh-keys — so use /ssh-keys/<key>, not the host path. Leave it blank to use the only key present. (The generated command below is meant to run on the host, so its -i path is the one place you want the host spelling.)
